Access was restored by switching the account to SMS-based MFA, which is now functioning reliably. The customer was provided with clear instructions on locating and downloading MFA backup codes to prevent future lockouts. Feedback regarding the lack of self-service MFA recovery outside business hours was documented and shared with internal teams for consideration. No further action was required, the customer did not respond to follow-ups, and the case has been formally closed.

summary: The customer contacted a member of our executive team to raise concerns about unsatisfactory support related to two major issues: Access to Evergreen Retainer functionality for the firm Limitations with Custom Roles when configuring user access
resolutionSummary: Access to Evergreen Retainer was granted to the firm. While this feature is not included in the customer’s current plan, it was enabled in this case because the plan limitation was not clearly documented in Clio’s external resources at the time. Help-CED: https://clio.slack.com/archives/C04AZDW2LFQ/p1767142331533959 I also followed up with our development team regarding the limitation discussed around Custom Roles. Specifically, the firm needs users to have full visibility into their Personal Dashboard metrics, including Hourly Metrics and Financial Metrics, without being granted access to Reports, the Firm Dashboard, or the Firm Feed. In short, the goal is for users to see only their own data, not firm-wide reporting. Our development team has confirmed this is a valid feature request and it has been formally captured for future consideration. At this time, there is no confirmed timeline for when this capability may be delivered, either this year or next year. We recognize the inconvenience this limitation creates for the firm. As a goodwill gesture, a 50% discount will be applied to the firm’s Clio subscription throughout 2026.

summary: The customer is requesting refunds for two separate concerns: Court Rules Jurisdictions The customer states she was charged for seven Court Rules jurisdictions that she claims she never added to her account. She is asking for a full credit/refund for these charges and is requesting proof showing when the jurisdictions were added and by whom. She also mentioned she did not receive any notification email about the charge and confirmed that nothing was found in her spam folder. Clio Grow Subscription The customer claims she requested cancellation of her Clio Grow subscription in October 2025, but continued to be billed. She is seeking a refund for those charges as well.
resolutionSummary: Following a comprehensive cross-team review involving Support, Subscriptions, and Communications, we confirmed that the additional court rule jurisdictions on the account were added in March 2022 under the customer’s user profile, at a time when no charges applied. The firm’s Essentials plan includes three jurisdictions, and advance notice of monetization for additional jurisdictions was sent via email on June 6, 2025, one month before charges began. Based on the account history, plan entitlements, and documented notification, the charges were applied in line with Clio’s policies, and no refund was approved.

summary: The customer is threatening legal action and requesting a full refund after signing up on September 26, 2025, specifically to use the GoTo integration for call and interaction logging. Despite support from Sales and Technical Escalations, the integration could not be completed due to required settings and permissions that must be enabled on GoTo’s side. The customer was informed of these requirements and advised to contact GoTo support, but declined to do so and instead requested cancellation and a full refund. As the issue originates from GoTo, a third-party integration outside of Clio’s control, and not from a failure of Clio’s product, the refund request for charges processed on September 26 and November 25 was denied in line with Clio’s Terms of Service and refund policy.
escalationDriver: False Expectations from Sales, Unsatisfactory Support Experience
resolutionSummary: After a comprehensive review involving Sales, Onboarding, and Technical teams, we determined that the customer’s inability to use the GoTo integration was due to required settings and permissions within the GoTo account, which Clio cannot control as it is a third-party integration. Clio provided guidance and troubleshooting support during onboarding and advised the firm to work directly with GoTo support to complete the setup, but the firm chose not to do so and instead requested cancellation and a full refund. As the issue originated on GoTo’s side and not from a failure of Clio’s product, the refund request was declined in accordance with Clio’s Terms of Service, with the option to receive support again if the subscription is reactivated in the future.

summary: The customer is threatening legal action against Clio and is requesting a full refund of $23,113.17 for their Clio Grow subscription. They claim the firm never knowingly subscribed to Grow, never used the product, and that someone without authority only attended a demo. They believe they have been billed since 2021, possibly as far back as 2019, without activation or use of the service. The customer states they received confirmation that the subscription was cancelled but were told a refund would not be issued per policy. They insist this is unacceptable given that, according to them, the account was never activated or intentionally purchased. A recent chat interaction reportedly confirmed their Grow subscription showed as “never activated,” which further escalated their concern. They are demanding intervention from senior leadership and expressing significant frustration with how the situation has been handled to date.
resolutionSummary: Our investigation shows that the Clio Grow subscription was created on July 30, 2019, and the cancellation was processed on December 25, 2025. At the time of cancellation, the account held four active licenses, with three active users and one pending user. We also reviewed the account’s historical activity and confirmed regular usage of Clio Grow. This includes the creation of contacts and matters, as well as forms being built and sent through the platform. This level of activity indicates that the subscription was actively used by the firm over the years. Given these findings, and in accordance with our Terms of Service, we are unable to approve the refund request. Our full ToS is available here: https://www.clio.com/tos/

summary: Eric Westman, the firm owner, is strongly objecting to Clio’s mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA) policy. He believes it limits his administrative control and could prevent him from accessing user accounts when staff are unavailable. Eric expressed frustration that Clio’s response felt generic and is demanding escalation to Clio’s senior leadership, including the CEO. His main concern is maintaining unrestricted administrative access to all firm user accounts, particularly in cases of employee absence or departure. He views the MFA requirement as unnecessary interference with firm operations.
firmName: Law Office of Christie B Mitchell
resolutionSummary: Email was sent to Eric to address his concerns about the mandatory Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requirement. The response acknowledged his frustration regarding administrative control over firm user accounts while explaining that MFA is a critical security measure introduced to protect customer account from cyberattacks and credential compromises. To help balance security with accessibility, recommended using 1Password, a secure credential management platform that allows firm owners to centrally manage all user logins and MFA details while maintaining administrative oversight. This solution ensures Eric can still access staff accounts when needed without compromising firm security. The resolution emphasized that MFA is not intended to limit access but to strengthen account protection across all firms using Clio.
